title: Teaching the Message of the Restoration (Part 2)
focus: Practice topic: teaching the First Vision
intro: God answered a boy’s prayer in a grove of trees and began the Restoration. In this lesson learners study the First Vision, see why it matters, and practise teaching it and inviting others to read the Book of Mormon.
preparation: Study Moroni 10:3–5 and Joseph Smith—History 1:1–19. Study President Gordon B. Hinckley, “The Marvelous Foundation of Our Faith,” general conference, October 2002. Prepare to share your own testimony of the First Vision. Pray for each learner by name.

sections.title: A testimony that reaches the heart
paras: Tell the story President Thomas S. Monson shared in “Come, All Ye Sons of God,” general conference, April 2013, about Elmer Pollard. A missionary’s simple testimony of the Prophet Joseph Smith reached his heart. Ask: Why did that testimony have such an effect? What does it teach about how we teach?

sections.title: Joseph Smith’s search
paras: Read Joseph Smith—History 1:5–9 and then Joseph Smith—History 1:10. Ask: What questions was Joseph asking? Why was it hard to choose a church? How are his questions like the questions people have today?

Read Joseph Smith—History 1:11–13 and James 1:5. Help learners say the truth: we can find spiritual truth by studying, asking God and acting on what we learn. Ask how they can use Joseph’s example to help someone else.

sections.title: The First Vision
paras: Let learners read Joseph Smith—History 1:14–19 on their own. Ask why the adversary would try to stop Joseph before he received the vision. Then ask what doctrines the vision teaches: the Father and the Son are two separate, glorified Beings, God hears and answers prayer, and the true Church was not on the earth.

Ask how the First Vision began to overcome the effects of the Great Apostasy, and why it matters that missionaries teach the story. President Gordon B. Hinckley taught that the whole strength of the Church rests on the reality of this vision (“The Marvelous Foundation of Our Faith,” general conference, October 2002). Ask why some people find it hard to accept, and how a missionary can respond with kindness and testimony.

sections.title: The pattern of the Restoration
paras: Connect this lesson to the last one. The Lord promised to restore all things in the dispensation of the fullness of times (see Ephesians 1:10). Ask how it helps an investigator to see that the Restoration follows a pattern God has used before.
Ask learners how they gained a testimony of the First Vision, and how that testimony affected their belief in the Restoration.

sections.title: Inviting others to read the Book of Mormon
paras: Read Moroni 10:3–5. Ask what steps a person takes to know the Book of Mormon is true: read, ponder, ask God with a sincere heart and real intent, and act on what is learned. Read Doctrine and Covenants 20:8–11 and ask why the book is strong evidence that Joseph Smith was a prophet.
Let learners watch for what makes an invitation work: care for the person, a clear invitation and a simple testimony. Then demonstrate introducing the book and inviting someone to read and pray.

steps.why: Teach the idea and why it matters for a missionary.

examples.title: List the truths of the First Vision
examples.text: Write on the board what the vision teaches: God the Father and Jesus Christ appeared, they are separate Beings, God answers prayer and the Church needed to be restored. Show each truth in Joseph Smith—History 1:16–19.

examples.title: Show how Joseph found truth
examples.text: Use Joseph Smith—History 1:11–13 to show four steps: study, ask, act, receive. Say how a missionary can follow the same steps.

examples.title: Connect it to the Apostasy
examples.text: Explain how the First Vision answers the Great Apostasy and begins the Restoration.

steps.why: Show one example of what learners will do.

examples.title: Teach the First Vision in three minutes
examples.text: Tell Joseph’s story in your own words, read Joseph Smith—History 1:16–17 and bear a simple testimony.

examples.title: Invite someone to read the Book of Mormon
examples.text: Show how to introduce the book, share its promise from Moroni 10:4–5 and invite a person to read and pray.

examples.title: Show an answer to a hard question
examples.text: A friend asks, “How do you know the First Vision happened?” Show how to answer kindly, point to prayer and the Book of Mormon, and testify.

steps.why: Learners practise in pairs or small groups.

examples.title: Teach in pairs
examples.text: Pairs prepare a four-minute lesson on the First Vision and the Restoration. Use your own words except when reading Joseph Smith—History 1:16–17. End with testimony.

examples.title: Invite in pairs
examples.text: Each learner introduces the Book of Mormon and invites a partner to read and pray. The partner shares a real concern.

examples.title: Share a testimony
examples.text: Each learner shares a short testimony of the First Vision with a partner. The partner says what felt sincere.

steps.why: Name what went well and what can improve.

examples.title: Partner feedback
examples.text: The learner who was taught says what was clearest and what felt most sincere. The teacher writes one thing to keep and one to improve.

examples.title: Three questions
examples.text: Ask: What went well? What would you change? What helped the listener most to understand the First Vision? Begin with the good.

examples.title: Simple checklist
examples.text: Was it simple? Was a scripture used and explained? Was the listener invited to act? Did the teacher speak with sincerity?

steps.why: Practise again with what was learned.

examples.title: Switch roles
examples.text: The learner who listened now teaches. Leave time for feedback both ways, then ask a few to share what they learned.

examples.title: Improve one thing
examples.text: Each learner teaches again and changes one thing from the feedback: a clearer sentence, a better scripture or a warmer invitation.

examples.title: Teach a new partner
examples.text: Find a new partner. Teach the same lesson again in a few minutes. Share one insight with the class.

testimony: Invite learners to share their testimony of the First Vision. Share your own and say that those who invite others to read the Book of Mormon will find joy.

tips.text: Help learners with hard questions calmly and faithfully, using official Church resources.
Let learners practise, then give kind feedback.
Ask learners to bear testimony of what they believe.
Tell the story first, then ask what the story teaches.

quote.text: This is My Beloved Son. Hear Him!

study: Read Joseph Smith—History 1:16–17 together and ask what the vision teaches about God.
invitations: Pray for a stronger testimony of the First Vision and the truth of the Book of Mormon.
Learn Joseph Smith—History 1:16–17 by heart. Share it with a friend or family member and add your testimony.
Pray for help to know someone who could receive a copy of the Book of Mormon.
